title: Open Problem: characterisation of ℓ-holed graphs for ℓ ∈ {4, 5, 6}
statement_text: Give a complete structural description of $\ell$-holed graphs (graphs in which every hole has length exactly $\ell$) with no clique cutset and no universal vertex for $\ell \in \{4, 5, 6\}$, analogous to the one the authors obtain for $\ell \geq 7$.
context_text: Graphs are finite and simple; a hole is an induced cycle of length at least four, and for $\ell\ge4$ a graph is $\ell$-holed if all its holes have length exactly $\ell$ (chordal graphs, which have no holes, are trivially $\ell$-holed). A clique cutset is a set $X$ inducing a complete graph such that $G\setminus X$ is disconnected, and a universal vertex is adjacent to all other vertices. Gluing two $\ell$-holed graphs along a clique, or adding a universal vertex, preserves being $\ell$-holed, so the task reduces to graphs with no clique cutset and no universal vertex. A bipartite graph between cliques $X,Y$ is a half-graph if $X$ and $Y$ can be ordered so that each vertex of one side is adjacent to an initial segment of the other side. A blow-up of an $\ell$-cycle has vertex set partitioned into non-empty cliques $W_1,\dots,W_\ell$, with edges only between cyclically consecutive $W_i$, each $G[W_{i-1},W_i]$ a half-graph and, for each $i$, $G[W_i,W_{i+1}]$ and $G[W_i,W_{i-1}]$ compatible (together a half-graph between $W_i$ and $W_{i-1}\cup W_{i+1}$). The authors prove that for $\ell\ge7$ a graph with no clique cutset and no universal vertex is $\ell$-holed if and only if it is a blow-up of an $\ell$-cycle or a blow-up of a more complex structure they call an $\ell$-framework (generalizing pyramids, thetas and prisms whose relevant paths all have the same length). They were not able to do this for $\ell=4,5,6$; for $\ell=5$, such graphs were studied in algebraic combinatorics and commutative algebra (Woodroofe), but no complete description is known.
